---
title: "Figure 5—figure supplement 2 — each member's distortion against the memory left in its own residual"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
FIGURE 5 SUPPLEMENT 1 (was figure_6BB.Rmd; renamed 2026-08-10 when the parent panel was promoted
to the body as Figure 5). Companion to figure_5.Rmd and to figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd: same data, one change, and it answers a
different question.

figure_5.Rmd and its two variants put EVERY member at the tau_int of the LEAST-SQUARES residual,
because that is the number a reader has in hand before choosing a method. A mark of IR at x = 17
there does not say that IR left memory 17 in anything; it says that in a cell where the classical fit
left memory 17, IR's distortion is 1.00.

AXIS FLIPPED 2026-08-27, when the body figure moved to 1 / tau_9: this panel now plots the
INVERSE of each member's own tau, so the two figures run the same way and the comparison the note
below asks for reads left to right in both. Nothing else changed.

THIS FILE plots each member at the tau_int of ITS OWN residual. That is no longer a decision panel,
since a reader cannot compute a member's residual without running it. It is a mechanism panel: it
asks whether the memory a member fails to remove predicts the information it then misreports. A
recursive member should sit near tau_int = 1 by construction, since the recursion subtracts at each
step what it has just seen, and whether it also sits near a distortion of 1 is the question.

READ THE TWO TOGETHER. If a member is clean in this panel and distorted in the other, its own
residual whiteness is not evidence that it is calibrated, which is the diagnostic blindness the paper
argues for in words.

Each panel has its own y scale, as in figure_5_variant_8members.Rmd, and its own x scale here as
well, because
the members' own tau_int ranges do not overlap.
Labels follow figure_4.Rmd:329.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE",
         macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
         macro_R = "R", macro_MR = "MR", macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")

# the only difference from figure_5_variant_8members.Rmd: tau_int is joined PER ALGORITHM
tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo %in% names(LAB)) %>%
  transmute(algo, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% names(LAB)) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("algo", "noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), is.finite(tau_int),
         mag > 0, aniso > 0, tau_int > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(unname(LAB[algo]), levels = unname(LAB)),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))))

cat(sprintf("figure_5_S2: %d marks; per member: %s\n", nrow(dat),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(dat$member), as.integer(table(dat$member))),
                  collapse = " ")))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.8}
g <- ggplot(dat, aes(1 / tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey45", linetype = "22") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ member, nrow = 2, scales = "free") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(Delta*t %.% k[off]), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("effective fraction of independent intervals in the member's own residual,  "*1/tau[9]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8))

ggsave("Figure_5_S2.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 4.8, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
cat("each member's OWN residual memory, and its distortion:\n")
dat %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            tau_med = median(tau_int), tau_min = min(tau_int), tau_max = max(tau_int),
            size_med = median(mag), size_max = max(mag), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nis own whiteness evidence of calibration? cells with tau_int < 1.05:\n")
dat %>% filter(tau_int < 1.05) %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(n_white = n(), frac_distorted = mean(mag >= 1.15),
            size_max = max(mag), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
